Currently, the principal balance on the loan is {$190000.00}. The construction loan required interest only payments during theconstructionphase. The interest only payments were on the {$190000.00} not the entire loan amount. I have now been informed, by WesBanco, that thebuilder has not met the deadline for the construction period and as a result, the allowed construction phase will end in XX/XX/XXXX and the principal balance and interest payments will begin in XX/XX/XXXX.

Based on the lot finishing sheet that was provided by the builders to WesBanco, $ XXXX is contingency funds that may or may not even be used, as we will not know the actual cost of construction until it begins over a year from now. 

Thequestion I pose : Is abanking institution allowed to require repayment on funds they have not actually disbursed to myself or any company on my behalf? In this case, {$600000.00} has never been disbursed and is still with the bank however, my monthly mortgage payment will be approximately {$3700.00}, to cover repayment for the non-disbursed funds.

Primary tabs ( a ) An instrument is transferred when it is delivered by a pi son other than its issuer for the purpose of giving to the person receiving delivery the right to enforce the instrument. ( b ) Transfer of an instrument, whether or not the transfer is a negotiation, vests in the transferee any right of the transferor to enforce the instrument, including any right as a holder in due course, but the transferee can not acquire rights of a holder in due course by a transfer, directly or indirectly, from a holder in due course if the transferee engaged in fraud or illegality affecting the instrument. ( c ) Unless otherwise agreed, if an instrument is transferred for value and the transferee does not become a holder because of lack of indorsement by the transferor, the transferee has a specifically enforceable right to the unqualified indorsement of the transferor, but negotiation of the instrument does not occur until the indorsement is made.
